audits.title: 77 National Audit of Care At the End of Life (NACEL)—Round Two Findings
audits.setting: Acute and community hospitals in England and Wales (175 trusts in England and 8 Welsh organisations); national comparative audit

cycle1.result: Possibility of dying documented in 88% of cases; 71% of Category 1 deaths had an individualised end of life care plan; median time from recognition of dying to death 41 hours; 80% of Quality Survey respondents rated care of the patient and 75% care of families as outstanding/excellent/good.

audits.other_findings: One-fifth of responses said families' needs were not asked about and 20% reported lack of peace and privacy; only 36% of hospitals had face-to-face specialist palliative care 8 hours a day, 7 days a week. First round median recognition-to-death time was 36 hours.
audits.citation: Hibbert D. 77 National Audit of Care At the End of Life (NACEL)—Round Two Findings. Age and Ageing. 2021;50(Supplement_1):i12-i42. doi:10.1093/ageing/afab030.38.

audits.title: End of life care in a secure hospital setting
audits.standard: LACDP 'One Chance to get it Right' five priorities for care of the dying person; tool adapted from the national End of Life Care Audit
audits.setting: Mallard ward, low secure psychiatric ward, Roseberry Park Hospital, Middlesbrough (TEWV NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: All three patients had documented recognition of dying, needs explored, individualised care plan followed and palliative care support; care largely consistent with the priorities.

audits.other_findings: End of life discussions were held with nominated persons rather than patients owing to lack of capacity.
audits.citation: Obasohan O, Tokas D, Kumari M. End of life care in a secure hospital setting. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S96-S96.

audits.title: Measuring the quality of end of life management in patients with advanced kidney disease: results from the pan-Thames renal audit group.
audits.standard: Quality markers of good end of life management
audits.setting: 10 hospitals in London and South-East England (pan-Thames renal audit group)

cycle1.result: Many aspects of good end of life care under-achieved; 69% of deaths were inpatient, 36% of these 'unexpected', with quality markers significantly less likely to be achieved in unexpected deaths.

audits.other_findings: Data collected over 8 weeks with a one-page proforma; trend to lower palliative care pathway use in ethnic minorities.
audits.citation: McAdoo SP, Brown EA, Chesser AM, Farrington K, Salisbury EM, pan-Thames renal audit group. Measuring the quality of end of life management in patients with advanced kidney disease: results from the pan-Thames renal audit group. Nephrol Dial Transplant. 2012;27(4):1548-1554. doi:10.1093/ndt/gfr514. PMID: 21980155.

audits.title: [Palliative care practices in residential facilities for the elderly requiring full-time care].
audits.standard: French Health Authority recommendations on palliative care
audits.setting: Larmont residential facility for the elderly (252 beds), Doubs

cycle1.result: Support person proposal recorded 27.6%; end-of-life instructions 23.2%; multidisciplinary procedure referenced 31.8% (compliant in under half); pain insufficiently assessed

audits.intervention: Quality improvement plan on patients' rights, anticipating end of life and pain management (not re-measured)
audits.other_findings: 95.8% died on the premises; discomfort other than pain identified in 89.2%.
audits.citation: Degois M, Grillot A, Boyraci E, Saillard V, Jandard AC, Prévalet-Courlet L, et al.. [Palliative care practices in residential facilities for the elderly requiring full-time care]. Sante Publique. 2015;27(2):199-204. doi:10.3917/spub.152.0199. PMID: 26414033.

audits.title: Using Audit to Improve End-of-Life Care in a Tertiary Cancer Centre.
audits.standard: Oxford Quality indicators for end-of-life care
audits.setting: Tertiary cancer centre, Cork University Hospital

cycle1.result: Exploration of patients' wishes documented in 24.2%; pastoral care referral 10.6%; poor end-of-life care in 21.2%.

audits.intervention: Care of the dying patient proforma, end-of-life care quality checklist, targeted staff education and training, and an expanded end-of-life committee (2022).

cycle2.result: Exploration of wishes 48.8%; pastoral care referral 68.3%; poor end-of-life care 8.3%; overall quality improved (χ2 (3, n = 138) = 9.75, p = 0.021).

audits.citation: Moloney CD, Carroll HK, Cunningham E, Nuzum D, Lyons M, Bambury RM, et al.. Using Audit to Improve End-of-Life Care in a Tertiary Cancer Centre. Curr Oncol. 2025;32(8):430. doi:10.3390/curroncol32080430. PMID: 40862799.

audits.title: Improving End-of-Life Care for Patients in Australian Cardiology Wards: A Retrospective Medical Record Audit.
audits.standard: National End-of-Life Care Standards (ACSQHC End-of-Life Audit Tool)
audits.setting: Cardiology wards in three Australian hospitals

cycle1.result: 64.7% recognised as dying; 134 had a documented resuscitation plan; 70% referred to palliative care; 8.7% (n=13) had an Advance Care Directive.

audits.other_findings: 76% (n=114) received active investigations or interventions in the last 48 hours of life.
audits.citation: Holman T, Macdonald P, Slade D, Goncharov L, Middleton S, Watts GJ, et al.. Improving End-of-Life Care for Patients in Australian Cardiology Wards: A Retrospective Medical Record Audit. Heart Lung Circ. 2026;35(6):845-854. doi:10.1016/j.hlc.2026.04.111. PMID: 42150968.

audits.title: End-of-life care and intensive care unit clinician involvement in a private acute care hospital: A retrospective descriptive medical record audit.
audits.standard: Australian National Standard for end-of-life care; 20 Processes of Care
audits.setting: Private acute care hospital (Epworth Healthcare), Melbourne

cycle1.result: Median 16 (IQR 13-17) of 20 care processes met; ICU clinicians involved in 65.7%; specialist palliative care in 53%.

audits.other_findings: ICU outreach contact or ICU admission was negatively associated with end-of-life care quality.
audits.citation: King A, Botti M, McKenzie DP, Barrett J, Bloomer MJ. End-of-life care and intensive care unit clinician involvement in a private acute care hospital: A retrospective descriptive medical record audit. Aust Crit Care. 2021;34(5):452-459. doi:10.1016/j.aucc.2020.10.010. PMID: 33358274.

audits.title: AN AUDIT OF PALLIATIVE CARE PRACTICES IN THE BRISTOL ROYAL INFIRMARY EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
audits.standard: College of Emergency Medicine (2012) end of life care guidelines (nine criteria)

cycle1.result: Died in ED: families involved 19/25, ceilings of treatment 23/25, DNAR forms 14/25, organ donation considered 23/25, bereavement services 20/25, end of life pathway 0/25. Died within 24 hours: families involved 13/25, ceilings in ED 10/25, DNAR 6/25, pathway 0/25.

audits.other_findings: ED met four measured indicators at over 80%; questions raised about end of life pathways and DNAR forms in the ED.
audits.citation: Yeomans D, Veysey S. AN AUDIT OF PALLIATIVE CARE PRACTICES IN THE BRISTOL ROYAL INFIRMARY EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT. BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care. 2014;4(Suppl 1):A71.2-A71. doi:10.1136/bmjspcare-2014-000654.202.

audits.title: A SUMMARY OF THE NATIONAL CARE OF THE DYING AUDIT FOR HOSPITALS, ENGLAND (NCDAH) 2013/14 AUDIT RESULTS
audits.standard: National Care of the Dying Audit for Hospitals standards

cycle1.result: Recognition of dying recorded in 87%; clinically assisted nutrition 45% and hydration 59%; spiritual needs assessment 21% (capable patients) and 25% (relatives); care after death 46%; 7-day SPCS access in 21% of hospitals; no audit in 44%.

audits.other_findings: 858 bereaved relatives responded (37%): most reported patients always treated with dignity by doctors (66%) and nurses (70%), and 76% felt supported.
audits.citation: Mulholland H, Gambles M, Lowe D, Husk J, Stewart K, Ellershaw J. A SUMMARY OF THE NATIONAL CARE OF THE DYING AUDIT FOR HOSPITALS, ENGLAND (NCDAH) 2013/14 AUDIT RESULTS. BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care. 2015;5(1):102.2-103. doi:10.1136/bmjspcare-2014-000838.4.
